title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

errors: In Corollary 2.6 (previous page), 'pour tout entier ℓ' should read 'for all primes ℓ ≠ char k'.

In the crossed-out chain the labels are inconsistent. In the first line σ: B_{X_{n-2}} → A_{X_{n-2}} and λ: A_{X_{n-2}} → A_X. In the second line the roles are swapped: λ is B_Y → A_Y and σ is A_Y → A_X. This is cosmetic only. Y = X_{n-2} is a surface, and the map λ on it uses the remaining class ξ_{n-1}|Y.

Equivalence (ii)⇔(i) on the next page tacitly uses that the pull-back of an ample (polarization) class under a homomorphism with finite kernel is again a polarization. This is true, but it is not stated here.

Only the existence of an inverse in Hom⊗Q is needed. Uniqueness and independence of ℓ follow because Hom(A,B)⊗Q injects into Hom of Tate modules. The page does not spell this out, but there is no gap.

ideas.what: Hard Lefschetz in degree 1 reduced to the statement that the map B_X → A_X = B_X^* induced by η is an isogeny, indeed a polarization
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture B / hard Lefschetz in degree 1 via Picard and Albanese varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil and Matsusaka (1950s); the degree-1 case of the standard conjectures is written up in Kleiman 1968, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures'
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968/69) notes that the conjectures hold in low degree / for curves and abelian varieties; details in Kleiman's Dix exposés

ideas.what: Factorization of u through a smooth surface section Y: B_X → B_Y → A_Y → A_X, with ρ and σ mutually dual isogenies by weak Lefschetz
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz hyperplane reduction for Picard/Albanese varieties

ideas.what: The correspondence homomorphism B_X → A_Y attached to a curve C → X×Y factors as v_{2*} ∘ φ_{Θ} ∘ v_1^*; equivalence of polarization, isogeny, finite kernel of v^* and surjectivity of v_*
ideas.modern_name: polarization of the Picard variety induced from the theta divisor of a complete-intersection curve's Jacobian

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard reduction of degree-1 hard Lefschetz to the classical polarization of the Picard variety via the Jacobian of a curve. It is well known and appears in Kleiman's exposition of the standard conjectures. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'est une isogénie, en somme, à un noyau fini' reads correctly; 'on peut' is inserted above the struck-out 'il faudrait'.
In the crossed-out chain the final arrow is labelled λ and the target is A_X; the scribbled 'A_{X_{n-2}}' is overwritten.
'σ l'injection' is uncertain. The intended meaning is that σ is induced by the inclusion Y ⊂ X (push-forward A_Y → A_X).
The whole boxed block from 'On est bien...' to '...l'une de l'autre)' is struck through with diagonal lines, not just the first line.
